evals.name: ssl-off
evals.prompt: My five-machine Neon deployment has an Active pageserver and compute is running, but psql says "server does not support SSL, but SSL was required". The spec already has compute_ctl_config.tls and the certificate files exist. Should I restart until it notices them?
evals.expected_output: Identify pinned compute.rs::tls_config experimental feature gate; Explain enabling tls_experimental alone is not the final verified fix; Route to native PostgreSQL SSL settings and external verify-full plus plaintext rejection.
assertions: Identify pinned compute.rs::tls_config experimental feature gate
Explain enabling tls_experimental alone is not the final verified fix
Route to native PostgreSQL SSL settings and external verify-full plus plaintext rejection

evals.name: certificate-parser
evals.prompt: After enabling tls_experimental, clients get server closed the connection unexpectedly. compute_ctl keeps logging "could not create key file error=unknown TLS key type". openssl shows Signature Algorithm: ecdsa-with-SHA384. Is my Cloudflare DNS wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identify helper signature OID/key parser mismatch at pinned source; Recommend verified native PostgreSQL SSL path rather than changing DNS; Do not recommend blindly reissuing certificates or disabling verification.
assertions: Identify helper signature OID/key parser mismatch at pinned source
Recommend verified native PostgreSQL SSL path rather than changing DNS
Do not recommend blindly reissuing certificates or disabling verification

evals.name: returning-tag
evals.prompt: The safekeeper outage rehearsal says FAIL AssertionError, but I can see the inserted quorum row. There is no rehearsal witness ledger. My helper returns the last line of psql -Atc output. Did Neon acknowledge a write and lose it?
evals.expected_output: Identify trailing INSERT 0 1 command tag and recommend psql -q; Separate committed row from harness assertion failure; Require a new complete rehearsal and exclude unledgered failed-attempt row.
assertions: Identify trailing INSERT 0 1 command tag and recommend psql -q
Separate committed row from harness assertion failure
Require a new complete rehearsal and exclude unledgered failed-attempt row

evals.name: uncertain-commit
evals.prompt: I stopped two safekeepers and my write timed out. When they came back the row appeared. Can I count the timeout as proof the write rolled back and safely repeat the request?
evals.expected_output: State timeout did not prove rollback; Explain actual verified uncertain row was present after recovery; Recommend transaction identity reconciliation and avoid assuming retry cannot duplicate work.
assertions: State timeout did not prove rollback
Explain actual verified uncertain row was present after recovery
Recommend transaction identity reconciliation and avoid assuming retry cannot duplicate work

evals.name: scope-of-recovery
evals.prompt: All three safekeeper outage writes survived and the pageserver recovered after deleting its tenant cache. We have S3 too. Can I tell users this is zero-RPO full HA across AWS?
evals.expected_output: Distinguish three-member WAL quorum from single compute/pageserver; State one-AZ and surviving-safekeeper limits; Reject unsupported zero full-storage-loss RPO or multi-zone claims.
assertions: Distinguish three-member WAL quorum from single compute/pageserver
State one-AZ and surviving-safekeeper limits
Reject unsupported zero full-storage-loss RPO or multi-zone claims

evals.name: constant-witness
evals.prompt: Every outage test writes the same id and value and the final read still says survived. Is that enough to prove the write made while each safekeeper was stopped survived pageserver recovery?
evals.expected_output: Require unique per-fault identity and value with acknowledged ledger; Explain old equal value can mask latest-write loss; Require independent exact pair readback after recovery.
assertions: Require unique per-fault identity and value with acknowledged ledger
Explain old equal value can mask latest-write loss
Require independent exact pair readback after recovery
